questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Combination of academic, career and culture but mostly the awesome nature where I could bike, hike, ski etc.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I chose my destination I initially wanted to go to the the southern hemisphere but felt that the US was a safer bet in regards to getting into the country during covid.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, CU Boulder had a very stremlined onboarding process for exchange students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None, figured most out on my own

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, I found my housing though the citys largest rental company. They seemed to have good availability. I chose one of their cheapest options which was still 1100$ a month.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is mostly freshmen that live on campus, so if you are older then you might not feel you fit in on campus. If you want to live off campus with a very stereotypical american college expirience then you should try to find private housing on "the hill" where all the student live and party.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Boulder is just very expensive and the realty companies do not seem to care much about the service they provide.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Good online portal, easy to find courses. Some courses take local students first though, so I did not get exactly the courses I wanted.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Everything is done online though an easy to use website that helps you plan everything

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Academic advisers are available at all their departments

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got 3/4 of the classes I wanted. the one I had to replace was replaced with another good class so no real complaints from me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you plan early so popular classes are not full

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Facilities and teachers are awesome at CU Boulder

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Final year BA. Took a 1000-, 3000- and two 4000-level courses. All of them electives

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more practically oriented. I studied at their engineering department, where as I study at the Science Faculty in Denmark.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CSCI 4413-001 Computer Security and Ethical Hacking
PHIL 1400-100 Philosophy and the Sciences
CSCI 4253-001 Datacenter Scale Computing - Methods, Systems and Techniques
CSCI 3202-001 Introduction to Artificial Intelligence

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the courses was great if you are interested in the subjects. CSCI 4413-001 Computer Security and Ethical Hacking is however a very difficult course, however if you get through it the teacher gives good grades.

Food DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: A lot of extra fees related to housing. The university also charges you to watch the sports games. A football season pass was 250$

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was a little more expensive than expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pretty much anything you'd like. There are clubs for anything you could imagine. These can be found online.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Clubs like the hiking club is great for meeting friends

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Skiing, cycling, hiking, roadtrips etc.
Colorado has endless adventure in the mountians

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. I was how ever used to american culture before coming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Make a good effort, some people are initially less interested in making friends when they know you are only there for a limited time.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No big differences that challenged.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How easy it is to talk to strangers in the US

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make a budget, it is expensive.
If you can buy/share a car that makes weekends more fun

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Avoid Four Star Realty if possible, but if not the just pay attention to your lease and charges.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Being a part of the cycling team and making many friends while cycling in the mountians.
The academics was also very rewarding, I feel I gained a lot of new competencies and knowledge.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping motivation high for school when there was so much to do and see

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
